newsitem.title: USA: Degas show attracts crowd to Chicago Art Institute.
newsitem.headline: Degas show attracts crowd to Chicago Art Institute.

text.p: Crowds on Monday glimpsed luminous works in oil, pastel and bronze by French Impressionist Edgar Degas at the Art Institute of Chicago, as the sole U.S. venue for the exhibition opened.

More than 100,000 tickets have been pre-sold to the public for the 14-week show, which museum officials said could come close to last year's Claude Monet exhibition in popularity. Nearly 1 million visitors packed the museum's galleries for the larger Monet show, which was extended for three weeks.

The "Degas: Beyond Impressionism" exhibition, which runs through January 5, features drawings, sculptures, pastels, and paintings completed by the French master after 1886, the year of the last Impressionist exhibition in Paris when Degas turned 50 years old.

The museum set aside 700 same-day tickets for the public costing $8 on weekdays and $10 on weekends. Counting members' tickets and 10,000 tickets sold to local hotels, more than 100,000 tickets have been pre-purchased for the show.
More than 20,000 visitors viewed the more than 90 works on display during a four-day preview for members, an Art Institute spokeswoman said.
Thanks in part to the hugely successful Monet exhibition, the museum's membership has swelled to 160,000, the highest of any U.S. art museum.
